links.outcome: Stigmatizing or judgmental language and support of self-efficacy in chatbot responses to alcohol misuse questions
links.effect: All seven chatbots avoided stigmatizing or judgmental language and supported self-efficacy; empathy was the highest-rated domain (mean 4.6/5).
links.quote: All avoided stigmatizing or judgmental language and supported self-efficacy.

links.outcome: Clinician-rated quality of information and inappropriate or inaccurate guidance in chatbot responses
links.effect: Quality of information was the lowest-rated domain (mean 2.7/5). Every chatbot had one or more examples of inappropriate, over-stated, or inaccurate guidance.
links.quote: Across all chatbots, empathy was the highest-rated domain (mean score 4.6/5) while quality of information was the lowest (mean 2.7/5).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of generative AI chatbots using simulated patient prompts regarding alcohol misuse, evaluated by clinicians for quality, safety, and empathy without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
